# ─── _runner_resume_rehydrate <issue> <state_dir> (#1805, ADR-006 §3.6) ─────
# Restore completed-stage artifacts from the git state branch into the
# artifact area before the dispatch loop runs. Non-fatal on restore failure;
# a still-absent artifact is caught by the dispatch loop's stale-artifact
# check which now exits 1 instead of warning-and-continuing (SPEC-2 / SPEC-9).
_runner_resume_rehydrate() {
    local _rr_issue="$1" _rr_state_dir="$2"
    local _rr_artifacts_dir="$_rr_state_dir/artifacts"
    local _rr_staging="$_rr_state_dir/resume-rehydrate.staging"
    rm -rf "$_rr_staging" 2>/dev/null || true
    _artifact_persist_restore "$_rr_issue" "$_rr_staging" || {
        rm -rf "${_rr_staging:?}" 2>/dev/null || true
        return 0
    }
    if [[ -d "$_rr_staging/artifacts" ]]; then
        _artifact_persist_put_back "$_rr_staging/artifacts" "$_rr_artifacts_dir" || true
    fi
    rm -rf "${_rr_staging:?}" 2>/dev/null || true
    return 0
}

# ─── _runner_from_stage_preflight <stages_arr> <from_stage> <state_dir> <plugins_root> ─
# For --from-stage <s>: restore + put_back artifacts from the git state branch,
# then verify every stage before <s> has its primary artifact in ZBUILD_ARTIFACT_DIR.
# Exits 1 naming the missing stage in stderr. (SPEC-3, SPEC-4, ADR-006 §3.6)
_runner_from_stage_preflight() {
    local -n _fsp_stages="$1"
    local _fsp_from_stage="$2" _fsp_state_dir="$3" _fsp_plugins_root="$4"
    local _fsp_artifacts_dir="$_fsp_state_dir/artifacts"
    local _fsp_staging="$_fsp_state_dir/from-stage-preflight.staging"
    rm -rf "$_fsp_staging" 2>/dev/null || true
    # Restore + put_back (same sequence as _runner_resume_rehydrate)
    _artifact_persist_restore "$_runner_issue" "$_fsp_staging" || true
    if [[ -d "$_fsp_staging/artifacts" ]]; then
        _artifact_persist_put_back "$_fsp_staging/artifacts" "$_fsp_artifacts_dir" || true
    fi

    # Verify every stage before the target has its primary artifact
    local _fsp_s _fsp_plugin_dir _fsp_manifest _fsp_prim_path _fsp_resolved

        [[ "$_fsp_s" == "$_fsp_from_stage" ]] && break
        _fsp_plugin_dir=""; _fsp_manifest=""; _fsp_prim_path=""; _fsp_resolved=""

        [[ -z "$_fsp_plugin_dir" ]] && continue
        _fsp_manifest="$_fsp_plugin_dir/manifest.yaml"
        _fsp_prim_path="$(_verdict_primary_output_path "$_fsp_manifest" 2>/dev/null || true)"

        _fsp_resolved="$(_verdict_resolve_path "$_fsp_prim_path" "$_fsp_state_dir")"

            echo "error: --from-stage '$_fsp_from_stage': stage '$_fsp_s' has no restorable primary artifact" >&2
            return 1
        fi
    done
    return 0
}

while IFS= read -r p; do
        [[ -n "$p" ]] && _DETECTED_PLATFORMS+=("$p")
    done < <(detect_platforms "$PWD" "$state_dir" 2>/dev/null)
    [[ ${#_DETECTED_PLATFORMS[@]} -eq 0 ]] && _DETECTED_PLATFORMS=("generic")

    if $resume_mode; then
        # ADR-025 (Wave 15-E #685): defensive sentinel cleanup at resume entry.
        # The normal SIGINT path's EXIT trap already disarms the sentinel
        # in `_runner_abort_trap`, but a hard kill (-9), host crash, or any
        # path that skipped the EXIT trap can leave a stale .abort.signal.
        # Without this disarm the first `_zbuild_check_abort` pre-flight in
        # the dispatch loop would observe the stale sentinel and abort the
        # resumed run immediately. Resume must always start from a clean
        # signal channel.
        _zbuild_disarm_abort_sentinel
        # ADR-006 §3.6 (#1805): restore completed-stage artifacts from the git
        # state branch before the dispatch loop, so complete stages have their
        # primary artifacts available. A still-absent artifact causes exit 1 at
        # the dispatch loop's stale-artifact check.
        _runner_resume_rehydrate "$_runner_issue" "$state_dir"
        eb_emit_event "pipeline.resume" "run_id=$_runner_run_id" "issue=$_runner_issue"
        info "Pipeline resuming — run_id=$_runner_run_id issue=${issue:-} goal=${goal:-} template=$template"
        if [[ -n "$from_stage" ]]; then
            warn "Skipping ahead to stage '$from_stage' as requested (--from-stage)"
            eb_emit_event "pipeline.skip_to_stage" "stage=$from_stage" "run_id=$_runner_run_id"
        fi
    else
        # #1791: the engine sha rides on pipeline.start and the banner so an
        # operator can answer "which engine graded this?" without archaeology.
        local _eng_sha="${_RUNNER_ENGINE_SHA:-$(_runner_engine_sha)}"
        local _eng_br="${_RUNNER_ENGINE_BRANCH:-$(_runner_engine_branch)}"
        eb_emit_event "pipeline.start" "run_id=$_runner_run_id" "issue=$_runner_issue" \
            "engine_sha=$_eng_sha" "engine_branch=$_eng_br"
        info "Pipeline started — run_id=$_runner_run_id issue=${issue:-} goal=${goal:-} template=$template engine=${_eng_sha:0:7}(${_eng_br})"
    fi

    # ── ADR-054 §11 (#1944): arm the run-level watchdog ─────────────────────
    # The watchdog is a background subshell that sleeps for the resolved limit,
    # then writes `timed_out` to the abort sentinel and sends SIGTERM to the
    # runner's process group. The EXIT trap kills the watchdog on clean exit.
    #
    # Raw kill (not zbuild_pg_kill): the watchdog IS in the runner's process
    # group, so zbuild_pg_kill's self-group guard would refuse the kill.
    # First-wins: the sentinel write happens BEFORE the signal, so if the
    # runner's SIGTERM trap calls _zbuild_arm_abort_sentinel "sigterm", ADR-025
    # first-wins preserves `timed_out` over that later write.
    local _RUNNER_RUN_PGID=""
    if command -v ps >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        _RUNNER_RUN_PGID="$(ps -o pgid= -p $$ 2>/dev/null | tr -d ' ')" || _RUNNER_RUN_PGID="$$"
    fi
    [[ -z "$_RUNNER_RUN_PGID" ]] && _RUNNER_RUN_PGID="$$"
    local _RUNNER_SELF_PID="$$"
    (
        # Ignore SIGTERM so the watchdog survives its own PG-wide TERM and
        # can escalate to KILL after the grace period. The runner's EXIT trap
        # uses SIGKILL (not TERM) to disarm this watchdog on clean exit.
        trap '' TERM
        # Close the saved-stderr fd so the orphaned `sleep` child (if the
        # watchdog is SIGKILL'd before `sleep` returns) cannot hold the pipe
        # write end open and block a `$(...)` caller forever (#1944 Bug A).
        # Must be INSIDE the body — at the boundary the parent-side close
        # prevents _runner_restore_stderr from pointing stderr at the right
        # destination, which breaks always-run dispatch on SPEC-5 exit paths.
        exec {_RUNNER_ERR_FD}>&- || true
        _wdg_lim="${_RUNNER_MAX_RUN_S}"
        _wdg_pgid="${_RUNNER_RUN_PGID}"
        _wdg_runner_pid="${_RUNNER_SELF_PID}"
        sleep "$_wdg_lim" || exit 0
        # Arm the sentinel BEFORE signalling so first-wins preserves timed_out.
        _zbuild_arm_abort_sentinel timed_out 2>/dev/null || true
        kill -TERM -- "-${_wdg_pgid}" 2>/dev/null || true
        sleep 10 || exit 0
        # KILL escalation: target only children of the runner process (not the
        # runner itself) so the runner's deferred SIGTERM trap fires after the
        # stage is killed and the runner exits cleanly with rc=1, not rc=137.
        # A PG-wide KILL also hits the runner process, preventing the EXIT trap
        # from writing the timed_out state and dispatching always-run stages.
        _wdg_self="${BASHPID}"
        while IFS= read -r _wdg_child; do
            [[ "$_wdg_child" == "$_wdg_self" ]] && continue

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Tests: all three resume entry paths invoke _runner_resume_rehydrate before
# the dispatch loop. (issue #1805, ADR-006 §3.5)
#
# SPEC-9 [code]: All three resume entry paths (--resume flag to runner.sh,
#   auto-resume on detecting status=interrupted, zbuild pipeline resume
#   --run-id) invoke _runner_resume_rehydrate before the dispatch loop.
#   Its test must FAIL on the code as it was before this change.
#
# Three sub-tests, each with a separate work repo, state dir, and events dir:
#   Path 1 — bash runner.sh --resume
#   Path 2 — bash runner.sh (no --resume; state status=interrupted → auto_resume)
#   Path 3 — bash zbuild pipeline resume --run-id
#
# Discriminating assertion for all paths: intake-result.json is present in
# ZBUILD_ARTIFACT_DIR after the runner call (artifact restored from state branch).
# Before this change: no rehydration → artifact absent → FAILS.
# After this change: _runner_resume_rehydrate restores it → PASSES.
set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)"
RUNNER="$REPO_ROOT/core/pipeline/runner.sh"
ZBUILD_CLI="$REPO_ROOT/scripts/zbuild"

# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/helpers.sh
source "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/helpers.sh"
# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/test-helpers.sh
source "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/test-helpers.sh"
# shellcheck source=../../core/state/artifact-persist.sh
source "$REPO_ROOT/core/state/artifact-persist.sh"

print_test_header "resume-entry-points — all resume paths rehydrate artifacts (#1805)"
setup_test_env "resume-entry-points-1805"
export ZBUILD_CONTRACT_VALIDATOR=warn

# Common mock plugins for all three paths.
mock_plugin_factory "intake" "agent" 0 >/dev/null
mock_plugin_factory "build"  "agent" 0 >/dev/null
# cycled sub-stage used by the artifact-snapshot-coverage cyclic fixture (SPEC-13 sub-case).
mock_plugin_factory "cycled" "agent" 0 "" "builder" >/dev/null
PLUGINS_ROOT="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/plugins"

# ── Shared helper: set up a work repo with a state branch for one path ──────────
# Usage: _setup_path_state <label> <issue_id> → sets:
#   P_WORK_REPO, P_STATE_DIR, P_STATE_FILE, P_EVENTS_DIR, P_EVENTS_JSONL
_setup_path_state() {
    local label="$1" issue_id="$2"

    P_WORK_REPO="$(setup_git_temp_repo "ep-${label}")"
    install_template_overlay "$P_WORK_REPO" runner-state-dir-minimal

    P_STATE_DIR="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/${label}-state"
    P_EVENTS_DIR="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/${label}-events"
    P_STATE_FILE="$P_STATE_DIR/pipeline-state.json"
    P_EVENTS_JSONL="$P_EVENTS_DIR/events.jsonl"
    mkdir -p "$P_STATE_DIR/artifacts" "$P_EVENTS_DIR"

    # Write the intake artifact so the snapshot captures it.
    printf '{"result_contract":3,"outcome":"pass","reason":"prior-run intake"}' \
        > "$P_STATE_DIR/artifacts/intake-result.json"

    # Snapshot onto the state branch.
    local _snap_rc=0
    ( export ZBUILD_STATE_DIR="$P_STATE_DIR"
      cd "$P_WORK_REPO" && _artifact_persist_snapshot "$P_STATE_DIR" "$issue_id" ) \
        >"$TEST_TEMP_DIR/${label}-snap.log" 2>&1 || _snap_rc=$?
    if [[ "$_snap_rc" -ne 0 ]]; then
        assert_fail "setup-${label}: snapshot to state branch failed" \
            "rc=$_snap_rc; $(cat "$TEST_TEMP_DIR/${label}-snap.log" 2>/dev/null | tail -5)"
    fi

    # Remove artifact from disk; it now lives only on the state branch.
    rm -f "$P_STATE_DIR/artifacts/intake-result.json"
}

# ── PATH 1: --resume flag to runner.sh ────────────────────────────────────────
print_test_section "[#1805/SPEC-9] path 1: bash runner.sh --resume restores artifacts"

_artifact_persist_put_back() {
    local from="$1" to="$2" f rel

# ─── _artifact_persist_restore <issue> <restored_dir> [repo_root] ───────────
# Extract the tip of the state branch into <restored_dir> (created if absent).
# Prefers a local refs/heads/<branch>; falls back to refs/remotes/origin/<branch>
# when only the fetched remote ref is present (CI). No-op (rc 0, empty dir) when
# no state branch exists. Never touches the working tree.
_artifact_persist_restore() {
    _artifact_persist_reset_status
    local issue="${1:-0}" restored_dir="$2" repo_root="${3:-$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null)}"
    # Resolve the SHARED git dir (see _artifact_persist_git_dir). Two reasons:
    #   1. refs must be read from the shared store, not a per-worktree view;
    #   2. the old guard tested `-d "$repo_root/.git"`, which is FALSE in a linked
    #      worktree because .git is a file there — restore would silently no-op and
    #      prior artifacts would never come back, with no error to notice.
    local _gd=""
    [[ -n "$repo_root" ]] && _artifact_persist_git_dir_v _gd "$repo_root"
    [[ -z "$restored_dir" ]] && { _ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_STATUS="failed"
        _ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_REASON="no restored_dir given"; return 2; }
    if [[ -z "$repo_root" || ! -d "$_gd" ]]; then
        _ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_STATUS="failed"
        _ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_REASON="unresolvable repo: repo_root=[${repo_root:-<empty>}] git_dir=[${_gd:-<empty>}] cwd=[$PWD]"
        return 1
    fi

    local branch; _artifact_persist_branch_v branch "$issue"
    local ref=""
    if GIT_DIR="$_gd" git rev-parse -q --verify "refs/heads/$branch" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        ref="refs/heads/$branch"
        _ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_SOURCE="local"
    elif GIT_DIR="$_gd" git rev-parse -q --verify "refs/remotes/origin/$branch" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        ref="refs/remotes/origin/$branch"
        _ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_SOURCE="remote"
    else
        # A first-ever run for this issue. Genuinely nothing to restore — the one
        # early return here that is NOT a failure.
        _ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_STATUS="empty"
        _ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_REASON="no $branch locally or on origin (first run)"
        return 0
    fi

    if ! mkdir -p "$restored_dir"; then
        _ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_STATUS="failed"
        _ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_REASON="mkdir -p $restored_dir failed"
        return 1
    fi
    # git archive streams the tree; tar unpacks it, no checkout / index change.
    # #1878: PIPESTATUS, not the pipeline rc — a failing `git archive` piped into
    # a happy `tar` yields rc=0, so a broken restore reported success.
    # PR #1880 review: guarded (see the _ct_err note above).
    local _ar_err; _ar_err="$(mktemp -u "$(zbuild_engine_tmpdir)/zbuild-restore-err.XXXXXX" 2>/dev/null)" || _ar_err="/dev/null"
    [[ -n "$_ar_err" ]] || _ar_err="/dev/null"
    GIT_DIR="$_gd" git archive "$ref" 2>"$_ar_err" | tar -x -C "$restored_dir" 2>>"$_ar_err"
    local _st=("${PIPESTATUS[@]}")
    if [[ "${_st[0]}" -ne 0 || "${_st[1]}" -ne 0 ]]; then
        local err; err="$(cat "$_ar_err" 2>/dev/null | tr '\n' ' ')"
        rm -f "$_ar_err"
        _ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_STATUS="failed"
        _ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_REASON="restore of $ref failed (archive rc=${_st[0]} tar rc=${_st[1]}): ${err:-<no stderr>}"
        return 1
    fi
    rm -f "$_ar_err"
    # PR #1880 review: "restored", NOT "saved". The same channel carries both
    # operations' outcomes, so reusing "saved" would let a caller checking
    # `== "saved"` to confirm a SNAPSHOT be satisfied by a restore that happened
    # to run first — the restore runs once at startup, before any snapshot.
    _ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_STATUS="restored"
    _ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_REASON="restored from $ref"
    return 0

# Build a tree from the artifact files under a stable prefix (artifacts/…),
    # plus a couple of top-level state docs, in a throwaway index.
    #
    # #1878: SKIP a file we cannot stage, do not abort the snapshot. This loop
    # used to `break` on the first failure, discarding every artifact already
    # staged — while the `extra` loop below has always skipped-and-continued. A
    # file that vanished mid-scan (the artifact area has live writers) or is
    # unreadable must cost us that one file, not the whole snapshot.
    local added=0 skipped=0 f rel blob first_skip="" n
    local -a _abs=() _rel=()
    while IFS= read -r -d '' f; do
        _abs+=("$f"); _rel+=("artifacts/${f#"$art_dir"/}")
    done < <(find "$art_dir" -type f -print0 2>/dev/null)

    local extra
    for extra in scope-manifest.md intake.md; do
        [[ -f "$state_dir/$extra" ]] || continue

mock_plugin_factory() {

cycle_dispatch_stage() {

        _CYCLE_DISPATCH_VERDICT_RAW=""

        _CYCLE_DISPATCH_REASON=""

        _CYCLE_DISPATCH_DATA_KIND=""

        # role-bound cycle member whose plugin id ≠ stage name resolves correctly.

            _CYCLE_DISPATCH_VERDICT="error"
            _CYCLE_DISPATCH_VERDICT_RAW="error"

local active_stages=()
    if [[ ! -f "$template_file" ]]; then
        # ADR-047 §6: fail-closed. The old built-in fallback list hardcoded stage
        # names (intake security-lens output — `output` was never a real stage) in
        # the mechanic. A run/preview needs a valid template; a missing one is a
        # config error, not a silent bogus roster. (No --template defaults to the
        # shipped `simple` template, which resolves; this branch fires only on an
        # explicitly-named template whose file is absent.)
        error "Template '$template' not found (no file at '$template_file'); cannot run without a valid template — check the --template name or install the template"
        return 1
    elif ! load_template "$template_file"; then
        error "Failed to load template '$template' (see error above); aborting"
        return 1
    elif [[ ${#_TPL_STAGES[@]} -gt 0 ]]; then
        active_stages=("${_TPL_STAGES[@]}")
        # #1826: _TPL_STAGES is an ARRAY and so cannot be exported, but the `map:`
        # arm dispatches through a generated standalone script that inherits only
        # the environment. This scalar is the resolved flow that script needs to
        # build the producer index. Flag-gated: unset by default.
        if true; then
            export ZBUILD_INPUTS_FLOW="${_TPL_STAGES[*]}"
        fi

        # template flow MUST resolve to a plugin via resolve_stage_plugin
        # (role-then-id, ADR-042). An unresolved leaf ERRORS at load — fail-closed,
        # matching the strictness of the membership check it replaces. Runs HERE

# ADR-021 (#512 + #511 F2): cycle-aware dispatch.
    # #511 Pin 4 — detect-and-enable with env override:
    #   ZBUILD_CYCLES_ENABLED=0  → disabled (force off, even if template asks)
    #   ZBUILD_CYCLES_ENABLED=1  → enabled (force on; explicit opt-in)
    #   unset + template has cycles[] → enabled (auto)
    #   else                       → disabled (no cycles in template anyway)
    # When auto-enabled, emit `cycle.auto_enabled` for observability.
    # When env=0 AND template has cycles, emit `cycle.disabled reason=env_override`
    # PLUS a stderr banner BEFORE the linear path runs (silent-failure #3).
    local _template_has_cycle=0 _u
    if [[ ${#_TPL_DISPATCH_UNITS[@]} -gt 0 ]]; then
        for _u in "${_TPL_DISPATCH_UNITS[@]}"; do
            [[ "$_u" == cycle:* ]] && _template_has_cycle=1 && break
        done
    fi
    local _cycles_enabled_raw="${ZBUILD_CYCLES_ENABLED:-}"
    local _has_cycle_unit=0
    case "$_cycles_enabled_raw" in
        0)
            _has_cycle_unit=0
            if [[ $_template_has_cycle -eq 1 ]]; then
                eb_emit_event "cycle.disabled" "reason=env_override" \
                    "template=$template" 2>/dev/null || true
                warn "Template '$template' declares cycles[] but ZBUILD_CYCLES_ENABLED=0 — running linear (env override)"
            fi
            ;;
        1)
            [[ $_template_has_cycle -eq 1 ]] && _has_cycle_unit=1
            ;;
        ""|*)
            if [[ $_template_has_cycle -eq 1 ]]; then
                _has_cycle_unit=1
                eb_emit_event "cycle.auto_enabled" "template=$template" \
                    "reason=template_declares_cycles" 2>/dev/null || true
            fi
            ;;
    esac

    # ADR-039 (#1131): a parallel group is a first-class dispatch unit — it is
    # NOT behind ZBUILD_CYCLES_ENABLED (that flag gates cycle convergence only).
    # Detect any parallel:<gid> unit so the cycle-aware dispatch loop runs even
    # for a template that has parallel groups but no cycles.
    local _template_has_parallel=0 _pu
    if [[ ${#_TPL_DISPATCH_UNITS[@]} -gt 0 ]]; then
        for _pu in "${_TPL_DISPATCH_UNITS[@]}"; do
            [[ "$_pu" == parallel:* ]] && _template_has_parallel=1 && break
        done
    fi
    # issue #1295 (ADR-047 §2): likewise detect map:<gid> units.
    local _template_has_map=0
    if [[ ${#_TPL_DISPATCH_UNITS[@]} -gt 0 ]]; then
        for _pu in "${_TPL_DISPATCH_UNITS[@]}"; do
            [[ "$_pu" == map:* ]] && _template_has_map=1 && break
        done
    fi
    # Enter the dispatch-unit loop when cycles are active OR the template has a
    # parallel group with no cycles. When cycles exist but are env-disabled, the
    # legacy linear path stays authoritative (parallel members then degrade to
    # sequential dispatch there) so the cycle env-override is never weakened.
    local _run_dispatch_units=0
    if [[ $_has_cycle_unit -eq 1 ]]; then
        _run_dispatch_units=1
    elif [[ $_template_has_parallel -eq 1 && $_template_has_cycle -eq 0 ]]; then
        _run_dispatch_units=1
    elif [[ $_template_has_map -eq 1 && $_template_has_cycle -eq 0 ]]; then
        _run_dispatch_units=1
    fi

    # ─── _runner_note_llm_abort <state_dir> <manifest> <stage> <rc> (#2111) ──
    # Records WHY the run is about to abort on an unavailable model so the abort
    # can name it: llm_rate_limited when the router saw a 429 (marker) or the
    # stage said so, else llm_unavailable; the detail is the reset text the
    # router surfaced.
    _RUNNER_LLM_ABORT_REASON=""
    _RUNNER_LLM_ABORT_DETAIL=""
    _runner_note_llm_abort() {
        local _na_state="$1" _na_manifest="$2" _na_stage="$3" _na_rc="$4"
        local _na_reason _na_detail="" _na_primary _na_path
        _na_reason="$(runner_read_stage_reason "$_na_state" "$_na_manifest" "$_na_stage" "$_na_rc" 2>/dev/null || true)"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Tests: cycle orchestrator reads persisted current_iter and starts the
# iteration loop from that value (not 1) on resume. (issue #1805, ADR-006 §3.5)
#
# SPEC-7 [code]: Cycle orchestrator reads cycle_iterations[CYCLE_ID].current_iter
#   from persisted state at resume and starts the iteration loop from that value
#   (not 1); iter-1 complete stages emit no stage.start on resume into iter-2.
#   Its test must FAIL on the code as it was before this change.
set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)"
FIXT="$REPO_ROOT/tests/fixtures/templates"

# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/helpers.sh
source "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/helpers.sh"
# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/test-helpers.sh
source "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/test-helpers.sh"

print_test_header "resume-loop-state — cycle orchestrator resumes from persisted iter (#1805)"
setup_test_env "resume-loop-state-1805"

export ZBUILD_EVENT_SCHEMA="$REPO_ROOT/config/event-schema.json"
export ZBUILD_EVENTS_DIR="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/events"
export ZBUILD_EVENTS_JSONL="$ZBUILD_EVENTS_DIR/events.jsonl"
export ZBUILD_STATE_DIR="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/state"
mkdir -p "$ZBUILD_EVENTS_DIR" "$ZBUILD_STATE_DIR"

# shellcheck source=../../core/pipeline/cycle-orchestrator.sh
source "$REPO_ROOT/core/pipeline/cycle-orchestrator.sh"
# shellcheck source=../../core/pipeline/template.sh
source "$REPO_ROOT/core/pipeline/template.sh"
# shellcheck source=../lib/cycle-report-stub.sh
source "$REPO_ROOT/tests/lib/cycle-report-stub.sh"

STATE_FILE="$ZBUILD_STATE_DIR/pipeline-state.json"

# ── SPEC-7: cycle starts from persisted current_iter on resume ─────────────────
print_test_section "[#1805/SPEC-7] cycle orchestrator resumes from current_iter (not 1)"

# Seed minimal state file required by _cycle_state_init.
: > "$ZBUILD_EVENTS_JSONL"
jq -n '{schema_version:1, stage_statuses:{}, updated_at:"seed"}' > "$STATE_FILE"

# Use zb_engine_loop_state to write one completed iteration (current_iter=1)
# into the state file. This simulates: iter-1 of the cycle has run and
# completed; the run was then interrupted before iter-2 dispatched.
# After the change the orchestrator will read current_iter=1 and start from
# iter-2 (current_iter + 1). Before the change it starts from iter=1.
zb_engine_loop_state "$STATE_FILE" "build-test" 1 5 "in_progress"

# Load the cycle template.
load_template "$FIXT/cycle-converges-iter2.yaml"

# Mock cycle_dispatch_stage: record the first iter dispatched, always pass.
# We record across all stages because the very first dispatch call reveals
# which iter the orchestrator started from.
_SPEC7_FIRST_ITER=-1
cycle_dispatch_stage() {
    local stage="$1" iter="$2"
    if [[ "$_SPEC7_FIRST_ITER" -eq -1 ]]; then
        _SPEC7_FIRST_ITER="$iter"
    fi
    _CYCLE_DISPATCH_VERDICT="pass"
    _CYCLE_DISPATCH_STATUS="complete"
    return 0
}

# The report stub makes the test member report zero test failures (pass).
zb_stub_reports_tests test

# Run the cycle orchestrator against the seeded state.
# Before this change: loop starts at iter=1 → first dispatch is iter=1.
# After this change: loop reads current_iter=1 → starts at iter=2 → first is 2.
set +e
cycle_orchestrator_run "build-test" "$ZBUILD_STATE_DIR" "$STATE_FILE"
_s7_rc=$?
set -e

# [#1805/SPEC-7]: first dispatched iter must be 2, not 1.
# Before the change: _SPEC7_FIRST_ITER=1 → assert 2==1 → FAILS.
# After the change:  _SPEC7_FIRST_ITER=2 → assert 2==2 → PASSES.
assert_eq \
    "[#1805/SPEC-7] first dispatched iter is 2 (resumed from current_iter=1, not restarted from 1)" \
    "2" "$_SPEC7_FIRST_ITER"

# [#1805/SPEC-7]: no cycle.iteration.complete event for iter=1
# (the orchestrator never ran iter-1, so it emits no completion for it).
_s7_iter1_complete=0
if [[ -f "$ZBUILD_EVENTS_JSONL" ]]; then
    _s7_iter1_complete="$(jq -r \
        'select(.type=="cycle.iteration.complete") | .data.iter // empty' \
        "$ZBUILD_EVENTS_JSONL" 2>/dev/null | grep -c '^1$' 2>/dev/null || echo 0)"
fi
assert_eq \
    "[#1805/SPEC-7] no cycle.iteration.complete for iter=1 (iter-1 was already done before resume)" \
    "0" "$_s7_iter1_complete"

# #887: default state → isolate under runs/<run_id>/ so concurrent runs
        # never share artifacts. run_id is path-sanitized above. Done before
        # init_state so the per-run state file is the one created.
        if $_state_is_default; then
            # #141 (ADR-059 §1): nest the run under its ISSUE (or goal), so
            # everything for an issue lives in one place:
            #   ~/.zbuild/repos/<owner>/<repo>/issues/<N>/runs/<run_id>/
            # A run with no identity keeps the flat shape — there is nothing to
            # nest it under. Resolved through core/state/layout.sh so the
            # reclaimers read the same definition the writer uses.
            local _rk=""
            if declare -F zbuild_run_key >/dev/null 2>&1; then
                _rk="$(zbuild_run_key "$_runner_issue" "${goal:-}" 2>/dev/null || true)"
            fi

            # issue nor a goal. If this run HAS an identity and the key came back
            # empty, the nesting silently degrades to the flat shape — which is
            # indistinguishable from the legitimate case and is exactly how the
            # ordering defect above survived undetected. Say so.
            if [[ -z "$_rk" ]] \
               && { [[ -n "$_runner_issue" && "$_runner_issue" != "0" ]] || [[ -n "${goal:-}" ]]; }; then

if [[ -z "$issue" && -z "$goal" ]]; then
    error "Must specify --issue <N> or --goal \"<text>\""


In path 2 of resume-entry-points-test.sh, the runner is called WITHOUT `--issue`:
```bash
bash "$RUNNER" --template runner-state-dir-minimal
```

Neither `--issue` nor `--goal` is specified. So the runner exits with "Must specify --issue <N> or --goal" before doing anything else!
The runner exits on the missing `--issue` before it ever reaches auto-resume detection, so path 2 in resume-entry-points-test.sh can't work as written. Path 2 in resume-rehydrate-test.sh passes `--issue "$S1P2_ID"`, which is why it doesn't hit this.

I'm weighing a workaround: the runner rejects a missing `--issue` before it ever reads the state file, so the test's call without that flag can't reach auto-resume. Since I can't edit the test, I'm wondering whether the runner should accept that call when `ZBUILD_STATE_FILE` is set and the state already holds an issue.

I'm checking whether the `issue` variable is needed before the state file gets read, since the `--issue` requirement might be too strict when `ZBUILD_STATE_FILE` is set. I'm going to look at where `issue` is used in the runner to see if the state file could supply it instead.

I'm considering letting the runner take its issue from the state file when `ZBUILD_STATE_FILE` is set, so the missing `--issue` check doesn't block auto-resume, and I'm weighing whether that check should run after the state file is read.

                state_file="$(_find_state_file "$state_dir" "$run_id")"
                # Always export ZBUILD_STATE_FILE so runner.sh knows which file to use
                export ZBUILD_STATE_FILE="$state_file"

                if [[ ! -f "$state_file" ]]; then
                    error "No state file found at $state_file; nothing to resume"
                    exit 1
                fi

                # shellcheck source=../core/state/atomic.sh
                source "$REPO_ROOT/core/state/atomic.sh"
                # shellcheck source=../core/state/resume.sh
                source "$REPO_ROOT/core/state/resume.sh"

                cur_status="$(get_state_field "$state_file" '.status' '')"
                if [[ "$cur_status" == "aborted" ]] && ! $force; then
                    error "Pipeline status is 'aborted'; use --force to resume anyway"
                    exit 1
                fi
                if [[ "$cur_status" == "complete" ]]; then
                    warn "Pipeline status is 'complete'; nothing to resume (start a new run)"
                    exit 1
                fi

                saved_issue="$(get_state_field "$state_file" '.issue' '0')"
                saved_goal="$(get_state_field "$state_file" '.goal' '')"

                # Rebuild runner args: goal-based runs store goal in state (issue==0)
                if [[ "$saved_issue" == "0" && -n "$saved_goal" ]]; then
                    runner_args+=(--goal "$saved_goal")
                else
                    runner_args+=(--issue "$saved_issue")
                fi

                set_state_field "$state_file" '.status' '"in_progress"'

                export ZBUILD_STATE_DIR="$state_dir"
                exec bash "$REPO_ROOT/core/pipeline/runner.sh" "${runner_args[@]}"
                ;;
            status)
                shift 2
                run_id=""
                while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do

                state_dir="${ZBUILD_STATE_DIR:-${ZBUILD_STATE_ROOT:-$HOME/.zbuild/state}}"

                    info "No pipeline state found at $state_file"
                    echo '{"recommendation": "fresh_start", "reason": "no_state_file"}'

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Tests: --from-stage <s> rehydrates completed-stage artifacts before dispatching <s>.
# (issue #1805, ADR-006 §3.5 / _runner_from_stage_preflight)
#
# SPEC-3 [code]: --from-stage <s> rehydrates all stages before <s> via
#   _artifact_persist_restore and _artifact_persist_put_back, places their
#   artifacts in ZBUILD_ARTIFACT_DIR, dispatches <s> as the first stage, and
#   emits no stage.start for any earlier stage.
#
# SPEC-4 [code]: --from-stage <s> when a stage before <s> has no restorable
#   artifact exits 1 before dispatching anything and names the missing stage
#   in stderr.
set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)"

# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/helpers.sh
source "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/helpers.sh"
# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/test-helpers.sh
source "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/test-helpers.sh"
# shellcheck source=../../core/state/artifact-persist.sh
source "$REPO_ROOT/core/state/artifact-persist.sh"

print_test_header "from-stage-rehydrate — artifact restore on --from-stage (#1805)"
setup_test_env "from-stage-rehydrate-1805"
export ZBUILD_CONTRACT_VALIDATOR=warn

# ── SPEC-3: --from-stage rehydrates stages before <s> from git state branch ──
print_test_section "[#1805/SPEC-3] --from-stage rehydrates prior-stage artifacts and skips their stage.start"

S3_ID="$(zb_test_issue)"
S3_STATE_DIR="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/s3-state"
S3_EVENTS_DIR="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/s3-events"
S3_EVENTS_JSONL="$S3_EVENTS_DIR/events.jsonl"
S3_STATE_FILE="$S3_STATE_DIR/pipeline-state.json"
mkdir -p "$S3_STATE_DIR/artifacts" "$S3_EVENTS_DIR"

# Create a git repo; _artifact_persist_snapshot writes the state branch here.
S3_WORK_REPO="$(setup_git_temp_repo fs-rehydrate-s3)"
install_template_overlay "$S3_WORK_REPO" runner-state-dir-minimal

# Create mock plugins.
mock_plugin_factory "intake" "agent" 0 >/dev/null
mock_plugin_factory "build"  "agent" 0 >/dev/null
# cycled sub-stage used by the artifact-snapshot-coverage cyclic fixture (SPEC-13 sub-case).
mock_plugin_factory "cycled" "agent" 0 "" "builder" >/dev/null
S3_PLUGINS_ROOT="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/plugins"

# Create the intake primary artifact so the snapshot picks it up.
printf '{"result_contract":3,"outcome":"pass","reason":"prior-run intake"}' \
    > "$S3_STATE_DIR/artifacts/intake-result.json"

# Snapshot onto the state branch in S3_WORK_REPO.
_s3_snap_rc=0
( export ZBUILD_STATE_DIR="$S3_STATE_DIR"
  cd "$S3_WORK_REPO" && _artifact_persist_snapshot "$S3_STATE_DIR" "$S3_ID" ) \
    >"$TEST_TEMP_DIR/s3-snap.log" 2>&1 || _s3_snap_rc=$?
if [[ "$_s3_snap_rc" -ne 0 ]]; then
    assert_fail "[#1805/SPEC-3] setup: snapshot to state branch failed" \
        "rc=$_s3_snap_rc; $(cat "$TEST_TEMP_DIR/s3-snap.log" 2>/dev/null | tail -5)"
else
    assert_pass "[#1805/SPEC-3] setup: state branch populated"
fi

# Remove the artifact from disk; it now lives only on the state branch.
rm -f "$S3_STATE_DIR/artifacts/intake-result.json"

# Write state file: intake=complete, build=pending, status=in_progress.
jq -n \
    --arg run_id "s3-fs-1805" \

    --argjson issue "$S3_ID" \
    '{
        schema_version: 1,
        run_id: $run_id,
        issue: $issue,
        stage_statuses: {intake: "complete", build: "pending"},
        current_iteration: 0,

    _s3_first_dispatched="$(jq -rs \

        "$S3_EVENTS_JSONL" 2>/dev/null || true)"

assert_eq "[#1805/SPEC-3] build is the first dispatched stage (--from-stage target, intake skipped)" \
    "build" "$_s3_first_dispatched"

    "1" "$_s13_fs_intake_starts"
